quests.instruction: Which fine, powdery ingredient is the main part of bread dough?
quests.hint: It is ground from grains like wheat.
quests.explanation: Flour is made by grinding grains, and it forms the body of bread dough. Salt and sugar are only added in small amounts for taste.
quests.funFact: Flour can also be made from rice, corn, oats and even chestnuts.

quests.instruction: Which ingredient makes cookies and cakes taste sweet?
quests.hint: A spoonful dissolves in warm tea.
quests.explanation: Sugar adds sweetness. Butter makes baked foods rich and salt brings out flavor.
quests.funFact: Sugar also helps cookies turn golden brown as they bake.

quests.instruction: Which tiny living ingredient makes bread dough puff up and grow bigger?
quests.hint: It is so small that you cannot see it without a microscope.
quests.explanation: Yeast feeds on sugars in the dough and gives off gas bubbles, which push the dough upward. Salt and butter do not do that.
quests.funFact: The gas bubbles from yeast leave tiny holes in bread, which is why it feels light and airy.

quests.instruction: A runny raw egg is cooked in a pan. What happens to it?
quests.hint: Think about a fried egg compared with a raw one.
quests.explanation: Heat makes the egg set, so the clear part turns white and the runny part turns firm.
quests.funFact: The clear part of a raw egg, called the white, turns solid white when it cooks.

quests.instruction: Which of these foods is usually cooked before people eat it?
quests.hint: Its tiny grains are hard when they are dry.
quests.explanation: Dry rice grains are too hard to chew, so they are cooked in water until soft. Grapes and cucumbers are eaten raw.
quests.funFact: Rice swells to about double or triple its dry size when it is cooked.

quests.instruction: What happens to a slice of bread when it goes into a toaster?
quests.hint: The heat dries it out.
quests.explanation: Toasting dries the bread and browns its surface, so it turns crisp and golden.
quests.funFact: Browning creates new flavors that plain bread does not have.

quests.instruction: Juice is poured into a mold with a stick and left in the freezer overnight. What does it become?
quests.hint: It gets cold enough to turn solid.
quests.explanation: Freezing turns liquid juice into solid ice. Jelly needs a setting ingredient and syrup stays a thick liquid.
quests.funFact: Water takes up a little more space when it freezes, so frozen juice swells slightly.

quests.instruction: Melted chocolate is poured into a mold and left to cool. What happens to it?
quests.hint: Cooling is the opposite of melting.
quests.explanation: As chocolate cools, the cocoa butter in it firms up again, so it turns solid.
quests.funFact: Chocolate makers heat and cool chocolate carefully to make it shiny and snappy.

quests.instruction: What rises from a pot of water when it is bubbling hot?
quests.hint: It is hot water that has turned into a gas.
quests.explanation: Boiling water turns into a gas called steam. Steam is very hot, so we keep a safe distance from the pot.
quests.funFact: Steam is invisible until it cools into tiny droplets, which we see as a white cloud.

quests.instruction: Which kitchen job blends ingredients together in a bowl using a spoon?
quests.hint: Picture going around in circles.
quests.explanation: Stirring mixes ingredients so they are spread evenly. Peeling takes off skin and freezing makes food cold.
quests.funFact: Stirring a pot on the stove also helps the heat spread evenly.

quests.instruction: A spoonful of sugar is stirred into warm water until it vanishes. What happened to the sugar?
quests.hint: You cannot see it any more, but you can taste it.
quests.explanation: The sugar dissolved, which means it broke into tiny pieces that spread through the water. The water tastes sweet because the sugar is still there.
quests.funFact: Sugar dissolves faster in warm water than in cold water.

quests.instruction: Cream is whisked quickly until it turns light and puffy. What did the whisking add to the cream?
quests.hint: Picture the tiny bubbles that make it puffy.
quests.explanation: Whisking traps tiny air bubbles in the cream, which makes it fluffy.
quests.funFact: Cream whips best when it is very cold.

quests.instruction: Which cooking method uses the dry heat of an oven to cook cakes and bread?
quests.hint: The food sits inside a hot box.
quests.explanation: Baking surrounds food with hot, dry air in an oven. Boiling uses bubbling water and freezing makes food cold.
quests.funFact: People have baked bread in clay or stone ovens for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which cooking method cooks food in water that is bubbling hot?
quests.hint: Bubbles rise and burst on the surface.
quests.explanation: Boiling cooks food in bubbling water. Baking uses an oven and frying uses hot oil.
quests.funFact: Water boils at a lower temperature high up on mountains, so food takes longer to cook there.

quests.instruction: Which cooking method cooks food in a pan with hot oil, and needs a grown-up's help?
quests.hint: It sizzles and pops.
quests.explanation: Frying uses hot oil, which can splatter, so a grown-up should do it. Boiling and steaming use water.
quests.funFact: Frying makes foods like fries crisp because the water on their surface turns to steam and escapes.

quests.instruction: Which method cooks dumplings gently using the hot steam from boiling water below them?
quests.hint: A basket sits above the water.
quests.explanation: Steaming cooks food with hot steam, so the dumplings stay soft and moist. Frying and baking use oil or oven heat.
quests.funFact: Bamboo baskets are a traditional steaming tool in Chinese cooking.

quests.instruction: Which of these foods is usually made by baking?
quests.hint: Dough goes into the oven and golden treats come out.
quests.explanation: Cookie dough is baked in an oven until it sets. Smoothies are blended and salads are mixed.
quests.funFact: Cookies spread and brown as the butter and sugar in them melt in the oven's heat.

quests.instruction: What food is often cooked outdoors on a grill over hot coals, with a grown-up in charge?
quests.hint: It gets brown marks and a smoky taste.
quests.explanation: Corn on the cob can be grilled, which adds a smoky flavor. Yogurt and pudding are not cooked on a grill.
quests.funFact: Grilled food gets its smoky taste from the heat and smoke of the fire.

quests.instruction: Which set of ingredients could be mixed together to make pancake batter?
quests.hint: The batter is thick enough to coat a spoon but runny enough to pour.
quests.explanation: Pancake batter is made of flour, milk and eggs. The other sets would make different foods.
quests.funFact: Pancake batter is runny enough to pour but thick enough to spread into a round.

quests.instruction: Oil and vinegar are shaken together in a jar. What are you making?
quests.hint: It goes on top of leaves.
quests.explanation: Oil and vinegar are the base of a simple salad dressing. Soup is cooked and ice cream is frozen.
quests.funFact: Oil and vinegar separate again if the dressing is left to rest.

quests.instruction: Which ingredient is often mashed into cooked potatoes to make them rich and creamy?
quests.hint: It is soft and yellow.
quests.explanation: Butter adds richness and a smooth feel to mashed potatoes. Lemon is sour and sugar is sweet.
quests.funFact: Butter is at least eighty percent fat.

quests.instruction: What do we call it when heat turns a solid food into a liquid?
quests.hint: Think of an ice cube on a warm day.
quests.explanation: Melting is when heat changes a solid into a liquid. Freezing is the opposite and baking cooks food in an oven.
quests.funFact: Cheese, butter and chocolate all melt when they get warm enough.

quests.instruction: What do we call it when a liquid gets cold enough to turn solid?
quests.hint: It happens in a freezer.
quests.explanation: Freezing turns a liquid into a solid. Boiling makes liquid bubble and melting turns solids into liquids.
quests.funFact: Water freezes into ice at zero degrees Celsius.

quests.instruction: Which sweet spread is made by cooking fruit with sugar until it thickens?
quests.hint: Strawberries and apricots are favorite fruits for it.
quests.explanation: Jam is cooked fruit and sugar. Butter comes from cream and honey comes from bees.
quests.funFact: Jam keeps well because the sugar helps stop spoilage germs from growing.

quests.instruction: Which list shows how to make a cheese sandwich, in the right order?
quests.correctAnswer: Take two slices of bread, add cheese, press the slices together 🥪
options: Add cheese, press the slices together, take two slices of bread 🥪
Take two slices of bread, add cheese, press the slices together 🥪
Press the slices together, add cheese, take two slices of bread 🥪
quests.hint: The bread comes first, because it holds the filling.
quests.explanation: You start with the bread, then add the filling, and last you close the sandwich.
quests.funFact: Sandwiches are popular lunchbox foods in many countries because they are easy to carry.

quests.instruction: What is the correct order of events when popcorn kernels pop?
quests.correctAnswer: Kernels get hot, steam builds up, kernels pop 🍿
options: Kernels get hot, steam builds up, kernels pop 🍿
Steam builds up, kernels pop, kernels get hot 🍿
Kernels pop, steam builds up, kernels get hot 🍿
quests.hint: Heat has to come first.
quests.explanation: Heat warms the kernel, the water inside turns to steam, and the pressure makes it burst open.
quests.funFact: Popcorn kernels need to hold a little moisture inside, or they will not pop.

quests.instruction: Put the pancake steps in order. Which list is right?
quests.correctAnswer: Mix the batter, pour it in a warm pan, flip it over 🥞
options: Flip it over, mix the batter, pour it in a warm pan 🥞
Pour it in a warm pan, flip it over, mix the batter 🥞
Mix the batter, pour it in a warm pan, flip it over 🥞
quests.hint: You cannot pour batter that has not been mixed yet.
quests.explanation: Batter has to be mixed first, then poured into the pan, and last it is turned over. A grown-up should handle the hot pan.
quests.funFact: Small bubbles that appear on top of a pancake show it is ready to flip.

quests.instruction: A baker mixes flour, water, salt and yeast, lets the dough rest and grow, and then bakes it. What does the baker make?
quests.hint: The dough gets bigger while it rests.
quests.explanation: Yeast makes the dough rise, and baking turns it into a loaf of bread. Pasta is boiled and pancakes are cooked in a pan.
quests.funFact: Bakers let dough rest and rise so that the bread turns out light and airy.

quests.instruction: What kitchen job should a child ask a grown-up to do?
quests.hint: Ask yourself which job involves something very hot.
quests.explanation: Hot trays and ovens can cause burns, so a grown-up should handle them. Mixing and washing cold foods are safer jobs.
quests.funFact: Oven mitts protect hands because they slow down how fast heat reaches the skin.

quests.instruction: Which ingredient would make a smoothie colder and thicker?
quests.hint: It comes out of the freezer.
quests.explanation: Frozen berries chill the smoothie and make it thick when they are blended. Hot water would warm it and oil would not help.
quests.funFact: Frozen fruit makes a smoothie thick without needing ice, which can water it down.
